subject: Urgent: Umbra Analytics - regional spike causing cross-region reroute request
messages:
From: Karen Li <karen@umbraanalytics.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-08T22:12:00-07:00
Subject: Spike in 5xx and latency - us-west-2

Rishi,

We started seeing a big spike in 5xx errors and end-to-end latency from our app hitting redwood in US-WEST-2 around 20:45 PDT. The errors are ~12% 502/504 and p95 latency doubled (now ~1.8s) over the last 30 minutes. Traffic volume is steady on our side — we haven't changed anything. Throughput has dropped by ~30% because of retries.

This is impacting our checkout flow for ~15% of users. Our ops team captured logs and a sample trace; attaching querylogs_20270508.txt and a screenshot of the 502s. Can you confirm whether there's an AZ/region event on your side, and whether you can divert traffic to another region? We need an ETA for remediation and any recommended temporary mitigations.

Karen
Karen Li
SRE Lead, Umbra Analytics
karen@umbraanalytics.com

Attachments: querylogs_20270508.txt
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Karen Li <karen@umbraanalytics.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-08T22:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx and latency - us-west-2

Karen — thanks for the alert and the logs, that helped. We're seeing elevated 5xx counts and kv-cache pressure on a subset of hosts in us-west-2 which correlates with increased tail latency and token-serve timeouts. Root cause triage is in flight with infra, but immediate mitigation plan below:

- Step 1 (now): Shift 60% of Umbra traffic from us-west-2 -> us-east-2 (same model variant pinned) via routing policy override; keep 40% on west for comparison.
- Step 2 (+15m): Enable conservative per-customer prefix caching and reduce batch sizes for Umbra to lower JVM memory pressure on the west hosts.
- Step 3 (+30-60m): If error rate drops below 2% on east, continue weight shift to 90% and then 100% if stable for 20m.
- Step 4: Postmortem + potential one-time credit if SLA hit confirmed.

We need Umbra sign-off to perform the cross-region steer. There will be a brief TTL increase for some sessions during migration; we will preserve model version and request idempotency headers. I'll copy Execs (Hannah/Marissa) for visibility and ask for credit/PRR guidance if we need to escalate.

If OK, I will kick off the route override now and provide minute-by-minute updates in this thread.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ops Response <ops@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-08T22:33:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Spike in 5xx and latency - us-west-2 (Umbra escalation)

Team — forwarding Umbra's report. Quick summary and asks:

Summary:
- External: Umbra Analytics reporting 12% 502/504s and p95 latency ~1.8s originating to us-west-2 (20:45 PDT start).
- Infra signals: kv-cache thrash and elevated token serve times on a subset of us-west-2 hosts; not yet a full AZ outage but host-level saturation.
- Business impact: Checkout failures for ~15% of Umbra users; likely urgent escalation to their product leadership in next 30–60m.

Immediate asks:
1) Ops: Authorize routing override to move 60% -> us-east-2 and perform rolling drain on affected west hosts. I will execute and monitor.
2) Finance/Rev Ops (Marissa): Please prepare a rapid assessment of one-time credit range if we confirm SLA breach (estimate: 5–10% of monthly invoice) — we may need to offer customer relief; I will not commit without leadership approval.
3) Hannah/Sean: Heads-up for exec comms; Umbra is a mid-enterprise account with active expansion discussions (deal UMB-2024-07). Prefer to keep primary exec outreach calm and factual; prepared a short customer-facing note once we have stabilization metrics.

Operational plan (2–60m) captured in the prior message. I'll perform the steer upon ops approval and report the results.

Forwarding original message below.

—Rishi
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Karen Li <karen@umbraanalytics.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-08T22:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx and latency - us-west-2

Karen / team — executing routing override now. Timeline and real-time updates below:

- 22:45 PDT: Initiated routing policy override for Umbra -> set us-west-2 weight 40%, us-east-2 weight 60%.
- 22:48 PDT: started per-customer prefix caching adjustments and reduced batch size for Umbra requests.
- 22:55 PDT: observed 5xx drop from ~12% -> 4.5% and p95 latency falling toward 1.1s. Throughput regained ~15% of lost requests.
- 23:10 PDT: shifted further to west 10% / east 90% after monitoring stability for 12m. Error rate now ~1.6%.

Attachments: screenshot_error_502.png (before/after heatmap).

Next steps: continuing to monitor for 60m, scheduling a bridge at 06:00 UTC for postmortem. I will coordinate a short customer note once we confirm sustained stability for 30m.

—Rishi
From: Karen Li <karen@umbraanalytics.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T04:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx and latency - us-west-2

Rishi — thanks for the quick action. We're seeing successful checkouts return and error rates down on our end. Appreciate the updates and the plan for a follow-up bridge and postmortem.

Karen
